trigger: the post-DELETE recheck of the deleted principal's auth.users.is_active in unassign_role's last-Administrator guard was a plain unlocked SELECT, so a reactivation (AuthDB::reactivate_user) committing between that read and the transaction's own COMMIT was unseen: the reactivated principal can already log in (AuthDB::get_user filters is_active = TRUE) and pass the admin gate, then loses its only Administrator grant when the unassign commits; the embedded OpenAPI text also claimed the window closed
summary: Fixed by taking a row lock on the single deleted principal's auth.users row in the recheck (SELECT is_active FROM auth.users WHERE username = $1 FOR UPDATE, WHERE deliberately username-only): a reactivation already committed is seen, one in flight makes the recheck wait and re-read its committed version, one starting later blocks until this transaction finishes. Design adjudicated by an enterprise-architect review and an independent second-model review, which both concluded FOR UPDATE on the deleted principal's own row is right (an earlier reading that the race only reaches a serial-order-permitted state was wrong: the login path observes the reactivated account before the grant disappears). Regression tests verified RED against the pre-fix code (fails at the blocked-backend poll, nothing ever waits) and GREEN: an in-flight reactivation that commits (refuses), one that rolls back (succeeds), one that commits with another Administrator present (succeeds), and a lock wait past lock_timeout (store fault, DELETE rolled back, not a refusal). Wording corrected in the OpenAPI text, rbac.md, audit-log.md, mcp.md, rest-api.md, the changelog fragment and code comments: closed for an existing account only; two residuals disclosed as NOT closed (an auth.users row created concurrently for a pre-provisioned grant, not tracked; deactivation of a surviving Administrator between the recount and COMMIT, #4966). Fix commits 7de64ae6d, 01bbc684e, 29d863779.
